title: The Establishment of a Public Defender’s Office
what_it_is: The Establishment of a Public Defender’s Office

sections.label: Government funding for criminal legal aid
sections.summary: The Government decided to directly fund criminal legal aid and CLAS, with changes made when funding was included.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2013, I gave a speech at the Association of Muslim Lawyers' Inaugural Lecture, and I announced that the Government had decided to directly fund criminal legal aid and we were studying how best to do it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In March 2015, I announced that the Government would fund CLAS; and for CLAS itself, when we got funding included, some changes were made.

sections.label: Plans and Public Defender's Office
sections.summary: In November 2020, the speaker shared plans, said the current model was not fully satisfactory, and that the Government prefers a Public Defender's Office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In November 2020, I shared some of our plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I said that we are not completely satisfied with our current model.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I also said that the Government, in principle, prefers the approach of a Public Defender's Office.

sections.label: Public Defender Scheme jurisdictions
sections.summary: Nine of the 11 jurisdictions surveyed have a Public Defender Scheme in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In nine of the 11 jurisdictions surveyed, a Public Defender Scheme is in place.

sections.label: Reasons for increased legal aid costs
sections.summary: Costs rose due to lack of robust means and merits assessment and overbilling by private lawyers, as in Hong Kong's 2016 legal aid spending.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There are various reasons for the increase in costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They include the lack of a robust means and merits assessment framework and safeguards as coverage expands invariably and inevitably.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, overbilling by private sector lawyers to whom criminal cases have been outsourced to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For example, in Hong Kong, S$217 million was spent on both civil and criminal legal aid in 2016, and that was due to continual increases in lawyers' fees of around 4% to 10% every year.

sections.label: Ontario legal budget cut
sections.summary: In 1996, Ontario cut its legal budget by 22% to control costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 1996, Ontario cut its legal budget by 22% to control costs.

sections.label: Preventing criminal legal aid abuse
sections.summary: A second concern is to prevent the abuse of the criminal legal aid system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A second concern, as I have said earlier, is to prevent the abuse of the criminal legal aid system.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office criminal legal aid
sections.summary: A Public Defender's Office will be set up to provide criminal legal aid, fully funded by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I will now share the next steps for this major change in approach for delivering criminal legal aid in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will set up a Public Defender's Office, or PDO, to provide criminal legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It will be fully funded by the Government.

sections.label: PDO under MinLaw
sections.summary: The PDO will be established as a department under MinLaw.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The PDO will be established as a department under MinLaw.

sections.label: Income coverage increase to 35th percentile
sections.summary: Income coverage will increase from the 25th to the 35th percentile, raising the per capita household income cut-off from $950 to $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our assessment is that we should increase this to the 35th percentile.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, we plan to increase income coverage from the 25th to the 35th percentile of resident households.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This raises the per capita household income cut-off from $950 to $1,500.

sections.label: Estimated criminal legal aid caseload increase
sections.summary: The total criminal legal aid caseload could increase by another 50% or a little more if take-up rises.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What does this expansion mean in terms of numbers?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We estimate that with these changes, the total caseload for criminal legal aid could increase by another 50%, or may be a little bit more, if the take-up rate for legal aid increases, and of course, this number could increase.

sections.label: Measures for sustainable aid costs
sections.summary: Measures will be put in place to ensure aid is given only in deserving cases and costs remain sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will have to be very careful to try and not strain the public purse.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We intend to put in place measures to try and ensure that aid is given only in deserving cases and try and ensure that the costs of criminal legal aid remain sustainable.

sections.label: Bill, PDO operations, funding questions
sections.summary: A Bill will codify the proposals and establish the PDO, aiming to start operations by the end of this year, with questions on funding and staff numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We want to enhance access to justice for vulnerable individuals in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will pass a Bill to codify these proposals and establish the Public Defender’s Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We aim to have the office start operations, at least in some modest way, by the end of this year, assuming the Bill gets passed in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of his concluding remarks as to when PDO will be established, which is towards the end of the year, can I inquire how much funding the office is likely to require?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second question is the number of staff PDO intends to raise to begin operations and, eventually, what is the number of staff that will be hired or appointed for the purposes outlined?

sections.label: Three headings cover nine laws
sections.summary: The three headings cover the nine pieces of legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The three headings cover the nine pieces of legislation.

sections.label: Funding from MinLaw budget
sections.summary: This primarily has to be funded out of MinLaw's budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On a more serious note, this primarily has to be funded out of MinLaw's budget.

sections.label: Private prosecution coverage principle
sections.summary: The thinking is that private prosecution should, in principle, not be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Again, I want to be careful about setting things in stone today.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But the thinking is that private prosecution should, in principle, not be covered by this.

sections.label: Appeals, LASCO and PDO coverage
sections.summary: It will cover appeals and both sides can appeal; whether LASCO is necessary depends on what PDO fully covers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the last one, the short answer is yes, it will cover appeals and both sides can appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On LASCO, I think one has got to see what PDO covers fully, then we have got to see whether LASCO is necessary because, in the end, regardless of which pocket, it all comes from the Government's pocket and, ultimately, from the taxpayer.

sections.label: Regulatory offences not covered
sections.summary: The intention is that regulatory offences should not be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our intention is that regulatory offences should not be covered.

sections.label: Serious offences and drink driving
sections.summary: Serious offences with serious consequences and substantive moral fault could possibly be covered; comments on drink driving are held until the list of legislation is settled.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If they are serious and they have serious consequences and they deal with substantive issues of moral fault, that is something that could possibly be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Drink driving, I am not quite sure where it fits in because it seemed to come from the third question.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I would prefer to hold my comments on drink driving until we have settled on the list of legislation.
